title: Bounded derived functors stabilize on the truncation tower

from.place: proof, first step, uniform upper truncation bound

statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $F:\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)\to\operatorname{Ab}$ be an additive functor on the category of sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] with right derived functors $RF$ and $R^pF$ [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. Let $N\geq0$ be an integer and assume $R^pF(\mathcal F)=0$ for every quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$ and every $p\geq N$. Let $E\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-derived-category] and, for every integer $n$, put $E_n=\tau_{\geq-n}E$ (standard truncation [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category]), with transition maps $E_n\to E_{n-1}$ the canonical ones. Then for all integers $i$ and $n$ with $n\geq N-i$ the induced map $H^i(RF(E_n))\to H^i(RF(E_{n-1}))$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 08D4 proof of part (2), truncation triangle H^{-n}(E)[n] -> E_n -> E_{n-1} and the two shifted vanishings

proof.text: For each integer n, the canonical lower-truncation triangle is $H^{-n}(E)[n]\to E_n\to E_{n-1}\to H^{-n}(E)[n+1]$ by [lem-pc-derived-lower-truncation-step-triangle].

source.place: Tag 08D4 proof of part (2), truncation triangle

proof.text: Applying the right derived functor RF, which is a triangulated functor on bounded below derived categories [lem-weil-pbc-derived-direct-image-triangulated] (all of $E_n$, $E_{n-1}$ and $H^{-n}(E)[n]$ are bounded below), to this triangle gives a distinguished triangle, and the long exact cohomology sequence [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] contains the segment $H^i(RF(H^{-n}(E)[n]))\to H^i(RF(E_n))\to H^i(RF(E_{n-1}))\to H^{i+1}(RF(H^{-n}(E)[n]))$.

source.place: Tag 08D4 proof of part (2), apply RF and use the long exact sequence

proof.text: By the shift identification for right derived functors [lem-sp-shift-identification], for every integer j the endpoint group $H^j(RF(H^{-n}(E)[n]))$ identifies with $R^{j+n}F(H^{-n}(E))$ when j+n\ge0, and is zero when j+n<0. Since $n\ge N-i$, both indices $i+n$ and $i+n+1$ are at least N, so the two endpoint groups around $H^i(RF(E_n))\to H^i(RF(E_{n-1}))$ vanish by the hypothesis $R^pF(\mathcal F)=0$ for p\ge N$.

source.place: Tag 08D4 proof of part (2), the two shifted derived-functor vanishings

proof.text: Exactness of the long sequence at the two middle terms, together with the vanishing of the adjacent endpoint groups from Step 3, makes the transition map $H^i(RF(E_n))\to H^i(RF(E_{n-1}))$ both injective and surjective, hence an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 08D4 proof of part (2), conclusion from the long exact sequence
